items.question: After finishing an associate degree, how do credits transfer to a Hong Kong university?
items.asker: — A Shandong student studying in Hong Kong
items.answer: Check the qualification level first, then the university's credit-transfer rules.
points: Compare QF Levels to confirm the courses are at the same level.
Check the target university's credit-transfer cap, eligible subjects and deadlines.
Confirm student visa renewal and accommodation so admission doesn't stall at the visa.

items.question: After my Top Talent Pass is approved, can my spouse and children come too?
items.asker: — A Jinan engineer preparing to work in Hong Kong
items.answer: Yes, via dependant visas, but documents differ by relationship.
points: Submit the main applicant and dependants together with relationship proof and a Hong Kong address.
Check the spouse's work and residence arrangements separately under dependant status.
For children's schooling, check school nets and application windows; secure a place before moving.

items.question: I registered a company in Shandong and want a Hong Kong corporate account. What comes first?
items.asker: — A Qingdao founder in cross-border trade
items.answer: Build the business-proof chain first, then book a bank appointment.
points: Prepare mainland entity, shareholding structure and beneficial-owner documents.
Organise Hong Kong contracts, invoices and transaction records to prove real operations.
Prepare address proof per the bank's pre-check, then book the interview.

items.question: My child has Hong Kong status. Should they return to the mainland or stay for DSE?
items.asker: — A Shandong family living between both places
items.answer: Confirm status and school records first, then compare the two timelines.
points: Check whether Hong Kong status, the Home Return Permit and mainland school records connect.
Compare DSE and mainland gaokao subjects, registration dates and admission rules.
Plan school nets, commute time and exam registration around where the family lives.

flow.sub: Not a pile of links — "ask clearly, find the source, prepare everything, finish it" broken into steps you can start today.

steps.label: Ask clearly
steps.title: Turn a vague wish into three answerable questions.
steps.body: "I want to develop there" is not a question. Identity, timing and budget are. State your situation so search and documents stay on track.

steps.label: Find the source
steps.title: Search official sources only, and show update dates.
steps.body: For policy questions, check government sites and official datasets first; keep the issuing body, source link and effective date in the answer. If there is no reliable source, we say so.

steps.label: Prepare everything
steps.title: Documents, forms and booking links in one checklist.
steps.body: List every requirement in application order so gaps are obvious. For forms, get field guidance and common rejection reasons in advance.

steps.label: Finish it
steps.title: On desktop, AI opens the official site and fills forms; you confirm each step.
steps.body: AI browser errands and document generation run on your computer. You confirm every click, entry and submission. Files stay local and are never uploaded.

mini.ask: I want to develop there, but I don't know where to start.
mini.docBody: Employed by a Hong Kong company or running a business there; pay and benefits must be at market level. Check the latest document list before submission.
